page: Microsoft Azure F64alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Faldsv7 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 64 dedicated physical cores running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz, with one thread per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 7559 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results place this server in the top 10% tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng, as well as in PassMark CPU and memory evaluations. The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, which contribute to its top-tier performance in cryptographic operations, software compilation, and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 11887.44 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 415.58 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

The primary tradeoff of the F64alds_v7 is its low memory density relative to its high compute capacity. While the 128.0 GB of RAM may limit memory-bound applications, the inclusion of a 7559 GB local NVMe SSD provides substantial high-speed storage capacity. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that require fast local scratch space but do not demand massive memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include compute-intensive tasks, web serving, software compilation, and small-to-medium language model inference.
description: Microsoft Azure F64alds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server from the Faldsv7 family, featuring 64 dedicated physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores running at 4.5 GHz. It is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, representing a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core, and includes a 7559 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance delivers top-tier performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng CPU benchmarks, PassMark scores, and memory bandwidth. The processor supports AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions, enabling rapid execution of vector and security operations. The main tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio, which makes this server less suitable for memory-intensive databases but highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy tasks. It is best suited for high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and small-to-medium LLM inference workloads.
